healthcareSystem: Mandatory universal health insurance system closely integrated with Switzerland. Residents must have health insurance. The country has one hospital (Landesspital) and excellent access to Swiss hospitals nearby.
qualityNotes: World-class healthcare leveraging Swiss medical infrastructure. The national hospital in Vaduz handles most cases, with complex procedures referred to Swiss university hospitals in Zurich, Bern, or St. Gallen. English is widely spoken by medical professionals.
pharmacyHours: Mon-Fri 8am-6:30pm, Sat 8am-12pm. Emergency pharmacy service available via hotline. Look for 'Apotheke'.
pharmacyTips: Well-stocked pharmacies similar to Switzerland. Pharmacists speak German and usually English. Swiss-standard medications available. Prices are comparable to Switzerland (high by international standards).
prescriptionRules: Swiss and EU/EEA prescriptions are accepted. Prescriptions from outside Europe may need verification by a local doctor. Same regulations as Switzerland apply.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Requires a prescription. Same rules as Switzerland apply.

restrictedMeds.name: Benzodiazepines
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled substances requiring prescription. Carry original prescription and doctor's letter.

restrictedMeds.name: Medical cannabis
restrictedMeds.note: Strictly controlled. Only available with local prescription for specific conditions.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English or German listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. EU/EEA citizens should carry their EHIC card.

travelInsurance.tips: Healthcare is very expensive (Swiss-level prices). EU/EEA citizens can use the EHIC for emergency care. Travel insurance with adequate medical coverage is strongly recommended for non-EU visitors. Helicopter rescue in alpine areas can cost 10,000+ CHF.

recommended: Tick-borne encephalitis (if hiking in rural areas)
vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations. Ensure routine vaccinations are current. Tick-borne encephalitis vaccination recommended for outdoor activities from April to October.

waterNotes: Tap water is safe and excellent quality throughout Liechtenstein. Mountain spring water is abundant.
foodSafetyTips: Excellent food safety standards identical to Switzerland. All restaurants adhere to strict hygiene regulations. No special precautions needed.
medicalTourismNote: Not a medical tourism destination due to its small size, but benefits from proximity to Swiss world-class medical facilities. Some visitors combine alpine wellness retreats with healthcare.
sources: Swiss Federal Office of Public Health
metaDescription: Health guide for Liechtenstein. Emergency numbers, pharmacy info, Swiss healthcare access, travel insurance tips, and vaccination advice.

hospitals.name: Liechtensteinisches Landesspital
hospitals.notes: The country's only hospital. Modern facility with emergency department, surgery, and internal medicine. Complex cases referred to Swiss hospitals.

hospitals.name: Kantonsspital St. Gallen
hospitals.notes: Major Swiss hospital frequently used by Liechtenstein residents for specialized care. Full range of medical services.

hospitals.name: Liechtenstein General Hospital
hospitals.notes: Government facility. Limited English. Bring a translator app.

dentalCare.availability: Several dental practices in Vaduz and surrounding towns. Swiss-quality dental care.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care is excellent but expensive (Swiss prices). Dentists speak German and usually English. No public dental coverage for tourists.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Dental clinics in Vaduz handle emergencies during business hours. After hours, contact Landesspital or cross into Switzerland.

mentalHealth.crisisLine: 143 (Die Dargebotene Hand / Tel 143 — emotional support hotline, German)
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Limited locally. English-speaking therapists available in nearby Swiss cities (Zurich, St. Gallen).
mentalHealth.notes: Small population means limited local mental health services. Swiss mental health infrastructure is readily accessible. Private therapists available in Vaduz.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Good accessibility standards aligned with Swiss norms. Modern buildings have wheelchair access.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Landesspital is fully wheelchair accessible with modern facilities.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Public buses (LIECHTENSTEINmobil) have low-floor vehicles. Mountainous terrain can be challenging.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Vaduz town center is relatively flat and accessible. Mountain paths and castles may not be accessible. Swiss accessibility standards apply.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: COVID testing available at Landesspital and local pharmacies.
covidStatus.notes: Healthcare capacity is excellent. Follows Swiss public health guidelines.

insuranceClaimProcess: Landesspital and private doctors provide detailed invoices. EU/EEA citizens can use EHIC for emergency treatment at public facilities. Non-EU visitors pay upfront and claim from travel insurance. Keep all receipts.

commonCosts.note: Healthcare costs are comparable to Switzerland — among the highest in the world. EHIC covers EU/EEA citizens for emergency care.

medicalEvacuation.note: Rega helicopter rescue covers Liechtenstein. For complex cases, transfer to Swiss university hospitals is standard. Short distances make evacuation straightforward.
